reasons: The cited deviation is real and correctly characterised: 14.2 says title vests 'Upon creation' yet is simultaneously 'subject to payment of the applicable Fees', an internal inconsistency that would let any fee dispute (including over unrelated amounts, given the broad 'Fees' definition) defeat our title to commissioned work product.

The redline is directionally correct and within the rule's scope (Customer ownership of Deliverables via Vendor assignment): it deletes the payment condition, leaves the assignment, personnel assignments and further-assurances language untouched, and creates no assignment of Customer IP/Data to Vendor and no joint ownership (consistent with deterministic checks 1 and 2).

The comment is accurate, cites the playbook position, and offers a sensible fallback (vesting on payment of undisputed Fees for the specific Deliverable); Vendor's payment protection via the suspension right is correctly noted, so the edit is not one-sided beyond the playbook.

Advisory minimality flag is explained by the short sentence rewrite, not scope creep; the only non-minimal element is the added belt-and-braces phrase 'and such ownership is not conditioned on payment of Fees', which is redundant once the condition is deleted and could be dropped to reduce negotiation friction — not a basis for rejection.
